svg.title: The multicast troubleshooting decision tree as six ordered questions, each with the check and the branch that stops the search
svg.desc: Six questions in fixed order, each paired with the command that answers it and the branch that ends the investigation. One: did the receiver join, checked with show ip igmp groups on the last hop router and show ip igmp snooping groups on the switch; if there is no entry, capture the IGMP report and check the host, the IGMP version and the ACL. Two: is there multicast state, checked with show ip mroute; a missing star entry means the join never went upstream or the RP is unreachable, and a star entry without a source entry means the source never registered. Three: is RPF correct, checked with show ip rpf; if the RPF interface differs from the real ingress, look at unicast routes, static mroutes, MBGP and ECMP. Four: did the traffic arrive, checked with mroute counts and interface counters; if not, walk upstream hop by hop or use mtrace. Five: is the outgoing interface list right, checked for the downstream interface and the Forward flag; a prune means the downstream never sent a join or a prune override was lost. Six: is the data plane forwarding, checked for exhausted multicast entries or replication resources, layer 2 forwarding by mirror capture, and MTU, fragmentation or QoS drops. A footer explains why the order matters: starting in the middle wastes the information that the earlier answers would have given.
svg.text: Six questions, always in this order - the last one is never the first one
The tree is a runbook, not a diagram. Each row is a command, and a branch that ends the search.

no (*,G): join never sent, or RP

empty. Walk up, hop by hop.
or a prune override was lost.
no L2 forward, or output drops.
Why the order is not negotiable: each answer eliminates half the remaining tree. Starting at RPF because it "usually is RPF" throws away the three facts
that the first two commands would have given you - and that is how a fifteen-minute fix becomes an all-night call.
